purpose: R255 HS300 200-day trend entry gate on the unchanged R253 nonfinancial weakest-link quality factor versus a matched quality-cash control

universe.industry_source: current ext_hy_ths industry snapshot; not historical PIT

factor.formula: hs300_above_ma200 = 1 if 000300.SH close_t > mean(close_{t-199}...close_t), else 0; null until 200 closes exist
factor.pit_rule: close and its trailing 200-trading-day mean are observable at t; execution is T+1 open
factor.missing_data_rule: exact-date join only; a missing gate date blocks new entries fail-closed

quality_factor.role: unchanged R253 cross-sectional ranking input, tested only on gate-on month ends

samples.rolling_1y: 252-trading-day rolling compounded return over the stitched 2023-2026 curve
samples.recent_12m: last 252 trading-day returns of the stitched 2023-2026 curve

execution.gate_scope: new entries only; existing positions remain subject to holding period and stop loss
execution.cost_stress: 4x and 5x scale all four components proportionally
execution.stitching: two segment returns compounded into one curve; first day of each later segment skipped

caveats: The gate blocks new entries only and cannot prevent losses on positions already open.
The 200-day rule is a fixed prior rather than an optimized parameter and may whipsaw near the average.
The gate is date-constant and has no cross-sectional alpha interpretation.
Conditional discovery IC has only several gate-on month ends and therefore low statistical power.
The underlying R253 quality factor retains financial-snapshot, current-industry and concentration risks.
This is another attempt in the same quality family, so multiple-comparison risk remains.
The full curve is stitched from two system-engine segments; segment boundaries can reset an open position.
Trade P&L shares are contribution diagnostics from two segments each starting at 1,000,000 notional.
Passing every gate would justify paper-trading validation, not production deployment.
